selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the passage’s main contrast between unbelief and belief?
questions.answer: Unbelief is presented as denial and lack of true knowledge, while belief is presented as real knowledge, affirmation, and sound judgement.

questions.question: How is belief linked to what is real?
questions.answer: Belief is linked to truth, real knowledge, and a correct conclusion about existence.

questions.question: Which is spiritually and intellectually weaker in the passage: mistaken acceptance or non-acceptance?
questions.answer: Non-acceptance is weaker because it is described as bare ignorance with no judgement behind it.

questions.question: What are the two basic kinds of convictions connected to unbelief in this passage?
questions.answer: One kind does not concern itself with the truths of Islam and follows its own false assumptions, while the other directly opposes the truths of faith.

questions.question: Which kind of unbelief does the passage focus on more closely?
questions.answer: The kind that directly resists and struggles against the truths of belief.

questions.question: What is meant by “non-acceptance” here?
questions.answer: It means not giving assent to the truth when it is presented.

questions.question: Why does accepting non-existence involve judgement?
questions.answer: Because the person is not just hesitating or refusing but actually choosing a position and holding to it.

questions.question: Why is universal denial of sacred truths impossible to verify?
questions.answer: Because no human can inspect everything in existence, the unseen world, and every time period in order to support such a claim.

questions.question: According to the passage, what lies at the core of unbelief that fights against Islam?
questions.answer: Its core is rejection, not knowing, and negation.

questions.question: What is the true nature of belief according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is real knowledge, affirmation, and sound judgement.

questions.question: What does the passage say belief uncovers when it rejects falsehood?
questions.answer: It uncovers or points toward a real truth.

questions.question: How many major categories of unbelieving conviction are given?
questions.answer: Two major categories are given.

questions.question: Why is non-acceptance easier than committed denial?
questions.answer: Because it does not require the person to build a defended position; it only requires refusal.

questions.question: Why is the first broad category not examined further?
questions.answer: Because the passage says it is outside the subject being discussed.

questions.question: What is the first type of negation named later in the passage?
questions.answer: Denial of a thing’s presence in a certain location or direction.

questions.question: In this passage, is unbelief treated mainly as a fuller knowledge or as a loss of true knowledge? Explain.
questions.answer: It is treated as a loss of true knowledge, because it is rooted in denial and ignorance even if it looks firm outwardly.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the positive side of belief even when belief rejects something false?
questions.answer: It says that when belief rejects falsehood, that rejection opens the way to a real truth or covers a truth waiting to be uncovered.

questions.question: What positive role does denial play within belief itself?
questions.answer: In belief, rejecting falsehood serves truth by opening the way to what is right.

questions.question: What is the first of the two broad kinds of unbelief described?
questions.answer: A type that does not pay attention to Islamic truths and stays within its own false assumptions.

questions.question: Which kind of unbelief is said to have no concern with the discussion?
questions.answer: The kind that follows its own false assumptions without directly taking up the truths of Islam.

questions.question: What is the second variety of the second basic kind of unbelief?
questions.answer: It is inwardly accepting non-existence and taking a side in favor of that denial.

questions.question: Which denial belongs outside the main argument because it can be demonstrated?
questions.answer: A limited denial about one thing not being in one place or direction.

questions.question: What attitude is described as “non-acceptance”?
questions.answer: Refusing to agree with truth when it is affirmed.

questions.question: What are the two broad categories of unbelieving conviction?
questions.answer: One is a false outlook not directly involved in the present dispute, and the other openly opposes the truths of belief.
